side_notes: All three agents operated almost exclusively at the sentence/clause level (sentence length, semicolon chaining, appositives, word choice). None examined paragraph-level structure: the ordering of the seven paragraphs, whether the findings/limitations/future-work sequencing itself adds load, or paragraph-to-paragraph transitions. That stratum is unexamined.

Coverage is heavily concentrated on P1 (opening), P2 (findings), P4 (takeaway), P5-P6 (limitations), and P7 (future work). P3 (robustness recap) drew only two findings (a2-f5, and a tail of a3-f4/a2-f9), so the robustness paragraph is comparatively under-probed relative to the others.

Several findings are guardrail_collision=true and sit on load-bearing caveat/qualifier content (causal-identification language, observational-equivalence of the two readings, powered-test-of-equivalence wording). These were kept per instruction; a human reviewer must confirm any future restyling does not erode the locked epistemic hedges.
